question: How the original feeds gfx/FX/arrow.fx for a selected unit's path: the vertices exactly (declaration, position, height, both texcoords, primitive, winding), what the head's distance is measured to, every parameter set by name and where it comes from, the technique and render states, when and in which layer the arrow is drawn, and the arrowType's class, keys and what each does.

addresses.name: CUnitArrow::Render
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnitArrow::Render(CUnitArrow* this, void* graphics, void* device, float* matrix, float time, int b, int c)
addresses.comment: **Slot 10: draws the arrow through gfx/FX/arrow.fx**, called by MapObjectGroup_Draw's no-mesh path (the type's slot 19 is ReturnZero). Reads only `graphics` of its arguments - not the matrix it is handed. The effect is graphics +0x6BD00 [type (+0x138) +0x140 - 1] (no test for 0); **SetTechnique("tec0")** with the name as the handle; Begin(&passes, 0). Then **twice**, i = 0 and 1: M = the arrow's world (+0x94); for i = 1, M._41 += map width (CMap +0x2A74, g_CMap 0x1A8557C) where M._41 <= 0, else -= it - so a second copy one map width east (the world's x is 0, so always east); **WorldViewProjectionMatrix = D3DXMatrixMultiply(D3DXMatrixMultiply(M, view (camera slot 91)), projection (slot 93))**, the camera at graphics +0x6BC88 -> +0x1C, the handle fetched by name; **CurrentProgress = +0x15C**, by name; **tex0** = the texture whose name is the type's `bodytexture` (+0x100), looked up in the graphics' map at +0x6B81C and read from the texture table (graphics +0x158 + index x 0x2C, +4), null where absent - so `textureFile` is not what is drawn; then for each pass BeginPass, VertexBuffer_Draw(+0x148) - SetFVF 0x202, stream stride 28, DrawIndexedPrimitive(TRIANGLESTRIP) - EndPass. End once at the end. `ret 0x18`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 11.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x87F770-0x87FA0F, every call: effect vtable +0xE8 SetTechnique with push 0x15E14FC 'tec0'; +0xFC Begin(…,0); +0x24 GetParameterByName 'WorldViewProjectionMatrix'/'CurrentProgress'; +0x98 SetMatrix; +0x78 SetFloat of [edi+0x15C]; +0xD0 SetTexture with push 0x15CFF6C 'tex0'; +0x100/+0x108 BeginPass/EndPass around call 0xAD4C30; +0x10C End. The loop counter [esp+0x14] runs 0..1; the shift at 0x87F810 reads [0x1A8557C]+0x2A74 and compares _41 with 0.0 (0x15BED10). IAT 0xD2B438 is D3DXMatrixMultiply (pefile). Wrong if a second caller passes a matrix this reads - [ebp+0xC..0x1C] are never read in the body.

addresses.name: CUnitArrow::BuildMesh
addresses.comment: **Makes the band of an arrow out of its points, as a triangle strip of 28-byte FVF vertices.** Frees the old holder (+0x148) and makes a new MeshBuffer (managed, primitive kind 1 = strip). With R real points (the points vector less the two added ends) and R >= 2, for each leg j between real points j and j+1, k = 0..19: p = D3DXVec3CatmullRom(point before, this, next, one after, k / 20), q = the same at k / 20 + 0.05; n = normalize(-(q-p).z, 0, (q-p).x); on the first leg across = n, from the second leg on across = normalize((n + the previous cut's n) * 0.5); A = p + 2 across, B = p - 2 across. **u** = 0.5, except that for the last 119 cuts only (cut number > total - 120) the straight 3D distance d from p (the cut's centre on the curve) to the **last real point** is taken and, where d <= 4, u = 0.5 + 0.5 x clamp(1 - d x 0.25, 0, 1). **v** = 0 at A and 0.5 at B. Each side is appended (ArrowVertexVector_PushBack) unless its position is within a squared distance of 0.001 of that side's last vertex, which is reused; the index of each goes onto a 16-bit list, **A then B every cut**. Afterwards each vertex's TEXCOORD0.x = floor(index / 2) / (indices / 2) - its cut's number over the number of cuts, the last (N-1)/N. Then VertexBuffer_Create(count, stride 0x1C, **FVF 0x202 = XYZ | TEX2**, not dynamic); the copy into the locked buffer sets each vertex's **height y = (0 where the province at pixel (trunc(x + 1.0), trunc(z + 0.5)) of CMap +0x20E0 (arrow +0x144 -> +0x1DC0) has is_land clear, else 0.02 - a missing province counts as land) + (0.62 where `overLand` else 0.05)**, no bounds test on the pixel; TEXCOORD0.y (+0x10) is never written. IndexBuffer_Create(indices) and the list copied in. So the strip draws 2 x cuts - 2 triangles. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, sections 10 and 11.

addresses.evidence: Listing 0x87FA30-0x880888. Cross product at 0x87FC03-0x87FCA5 gives (0*dy - dz, 0, dx - 0*dy); averaging gated by cmp [ebp-0x3C],1 at 0x87FCFC. A from [ebp-0x70..-0x68] = p + 2.0 (0x160A360) x across with v [ebp-0xBC] = 0 (0x880205); B from [ebp-0x7C..-0x74] with v [ebp-0xD8] = 0.5 (0x15AB304). Head gate cmp edx,[ebp-0x54] at 0x87FF85 with [ebp-0x54] = 20(N-2) - 120; distance to [[edi+0x14C] + [ebp-0x38]*12] at 0x87FF91, 4.0 at 0x171DF34, 0.25 at 0x160A258. Dedup threshold 0.001 (0x171DF30) against FloatAbs of the squared length. Progress loop 0x880630-0x880669 writes [vertex+0xC]. VertexBuffer_Create pushes 0, 0x202, 0x1C at 0x880689; holder kind [eax+0x20] = 1 at 0x87FAD2. addresses.name: CUnitArrow::CUnitArrow
addresses.no_signature: the type in ECX and six stack arguments: the object, the graphics, the object layer, the graphics owner, the list of points, and overLand; `ret 0x18`, the object returned in EAX
addresses.comment: The arrow's constructor: the C3dVisibleObject constructor with the type (so the type is at +0xF8 as well as +0x138), the table at VA 0x15E3C14, **the graphics at +0x13C, the object layer at +0x140 and +0xE8 (the scene), the graphics owner at +0x144**, the mesh pointer cleared and +0x15C = 0. Then it walks the doubly linked list of points (nodes of x, y, z, prev +0xC, next +0x10): the first and last nodes are always copied into the vector at +0x14C; any other node whose x, y and z each lie within 0.1 of the next node's is dropped **and the next node is passed over as well** (neither is copied); every other node is copied - a test of the turn's angle follows, but its threshold is -500 degrees and acos x 57.3 is never below it, so it never removes a point. Ends with CUnitArrow::BuildMesh(this, overLand). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, sections 10 and 11.
addresses.revises: Corrects 'a point within 0.1 of the next is dropped': the next point is skipped too, the first and last are always kept, and the angle test is dead. Adds the three pointer arguments and where they land.

The close test at 0x87F2FA-0x87F39C compares FloatAbs of each difference with 0.1 (0x160A3C0) and then does mov ebx,[ebx+0x10] at 0x87F39E before the loop's own mov ebx,[ebx+0x10] at 0x87F605. MakeArrow passes is_land of the unit's current province (0x5CCBFD).

addresses.name: CUnit::MakeArrow
addresses.comment: **Makes the arrow drawn along a selected unit's way.** Null for a unit with no graphics owner or no path. Its points are the unit's own place - its stack's point plus the province's label point - and the unit point of every province of the path, x moved by the map's width where that is the short way round, each with a height of 0.02 over land and 0 over sea (BuildMesh replaces the heights); a fleet starts and ends at a naval base position where it is in a land province, a wing at an air base. A point is added 5 beyond each end in line with the end's leg. The type is looked up by name in the graphics' object-type registry (+0x6BCF0): `unitInvasionArrow` where 0x5C2E80(unit, 1) says so, `retreatArrow` where retreating (+0x158), `attackArrow` where CUnit::IsNextProvinceEnemyHeld, `stratArrow` under order type 0x5A4, else `moveArrow`. Then `new 0x160` and the CUnitArrow constructor with (graphics, the owner's layer at +0x8F4, the graphics owner - the idler's slot 15 -, the points, is_land of the unit's current province). **Placing it**: C3dObject::Translate by (-label_x, -0.52, -label_y) of the current province (template +0x5C/+0x60), UpdateTransform, added to the layer (its slot 4), and ProvinceGraphics_PlacePicture on that province with raise - which adds 1.0 to the height and makes the world = local x the province anchor's world; with the anchor at (centre, 0) on land and (label, 0.3) at sea and the label a copy of the centre, **the arrow's world is a translation by (0, 0.48, 0) on land and (0, 0.78, 0) at sea**. Then the unit's arrow_state (+0x18C) is stepped and handed to the arrow's slot 23, which for an arrow does nothing; +0x15C = movement_progress over CUnit::PathDistance; Show (slot 13). Callers: CUnit::ShowMoving, CUnit::EnterProvince, CUnit::OnSelected, CUnit::ShowFighting and CUnit::ShowCombatOver - each for a selected unit (CUnit +4) - and CUnit::RemakeArrow. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, sections 10 and 11.
addresses.revises: Adds the arguments to the constructor, the placement on the province anchor that puts the whole arrow 0.48 (land) or 0.78 (sea) up, the Show call, and three callers the entry did not list (OnSelected, ShowFighting, ShowCombatOver).
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5CCB37-0x5CCE29: StringHashFind on [owner slot 17]+0x6BCF0; constructor pushes at 0x5CCC2E-0x5CCC51; C3dObject::Translate (slot 33, +0x84) at 0x5CCCCD with (-(float)[tmpl+0x5C], -0.52 (0x160A8D8), -(float)[tmpl+0x60]); slot 44 at 0x5CCCD9; layer slot 4 at 0x5CCCEC; call 0x640CA0 with push 1 at 0x5CCD1A; +0x15C stored at 0x5CCE21; slot 13 (+0x34) at 0x5CCE29. findRefs --callers 0x5CC230: 0x5BFB07, 0x5C0646, 0x5C7C46, 0x5C8070, 0x5CA100, 0x5CC21A; the ShowFighting and ShowCombatOver sites test byte [ebx+4] first. structs.name: CArrowType
structs.comment: An `arrowType` of interface/arrows.gfx (moveArrow, stratArrow, attackArrow, retreatArrow, unitInvasionArrow, invasionArrow, AutomationArrow, OtherAutomationArrow, convoyArrow1/2). No RTTI - the table at VA 0x16051A0 has no complete-object locator - so the name is ours.
